findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `get_item_key` receives an `AuditLogEntry.datetime` value. This implementation calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on that `datetime`, which raises `TypeError` when `build_cursor` processes the first page. Consequently, any authorized request using `optimized_pagination=true` will return a 500 rather than audit-log results. The optimized paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible datetime cursor conversion (or must inherit/use that implementation).

findings.title: Advanced negative cursor offsets cause Django queryset slicing errors
findings.body: The advanced path passes a negative `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing/slicing and raise an error; they do not handle it automatically as the comment states. Since cursor offsets are parsed from client-provided cursor strings, an authorized caller can trigger a 500 with a negative offset while `optimized_pagination=true` is enabled. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a valid query rather than passed to a QuerySet slice.
